title: Bhindi (Ladies Finger): modeled ₹532/qtl left, Kottayam → Angamaly
summary: March 2021: reported bhindi (Ladies Finger) prices at Kottayam and Angamaly imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 92% of 24 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹532 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 992 same-variety market pairs screened for bhindi (Ladies Finger) in March 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Bhindi, FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Angamaly report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: March 2021
scenes.caption: Kottayam (Kerala) and Angamaly (Kerala) both reported bhindi (Ladies Finger) prices for the same variety and grade (Bhindi, FAQ) on 24 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kottayam reported a median ₹2,050 per quintal. Angamaly reported a median ₹3,000 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹700/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹700 per quintal, and Angamaly was dearer on 92% of days.

scenes.headline: 87 km by road
scenes.caption: 87 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹19/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹296 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹140 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Angamaly report, the rule selects 24 of 24 modeled shipping days. 22 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹532 per quintal (₹360 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Bhindi (Ladies Finger) route from Kottayam to Angamaly was positive on 92% of matched days in March 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹53,200, or ₹36,000 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to bhindi (Ladies Finger)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹19/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Bhindi (Ladies Finger) route from Kottayam to Angamaly was positive on 92% of matched days in March 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹53,200, or ₹36,000 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
